review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how `conePullback_obj` and `conePullback_map` are used elsewhere in the repo: ConePullbackCocone.lean, AbelianForget/ConePullback.lean, CommRingForget/ConePullback.lean and SheafCohomologyExamples. I did not report simp annotations for the algebraic lemmas (`sheafMate_id`, `sheafMate_comp`, `triangleMap_id`, `triangleMap_comp`, `pullbackCompInv_assoc`). They are not clearly canonical rewrites: the `triangleMap` lemmas carry triangle-proof arguments, and `triangleMap_comp` and `pullbackCompInv_assoc` have no obvious normal-form direction. I did not run Lean, so the competition between `conePullback_map` and `Functor.map_id`/`Functor.map_comp` is a reasoned concern, not an observed failure. The existing uses all rewrite or simp this lemma at generic `a`, so they are probably unaffected by the change.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem conePullback_map (S : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafedSpace A)
    (c : Cone (S ⋙ forget A)) {i j : J} (a : i ⟶ j) :
    (conePullback A S c).map a =
      triangleMap A
findings.problem: `conePullback_map` is a `@[simp]` lemma whose left side is the fully generic `(conePullback A S c).map a`. It therefore also matches `(conePullback A S c).map (𝟙 i)` and `(conePullback A S c).map (a ≫ b)`, which `Functor.map_id` and `Functor.map_comp` already handle. This is a competing-rules problem. Which rule fires first is not controlled by priority or specificity. If this one fires, the result is `triangleMap … (sheafMate A (S.map (𝟙 i).op))`. The correct normal form is `𝟙 _` (or a composite of two maps). That unfolded form is then only recoverable by hand, through `conePullbackMap_id`/`conePullbackMap_comp`, which are not simp lemmas. The right-hand sides of `conePullback_obj` and `conePullback_map` also unfold to the raw `pullback`/`triangleMap … sheafMate` terms instead of the named `conePullbackObj`/`conePullbackMap` definitions. Those definitions are the ones other files use, for example `(SheafedSpace.conePullbackMap (Type v) N c g).hom.naturality` in NativeStageSectionLifting.lean. Unfolding to the raw terms loses the abstraction boundary.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `conePullback_obj` and `conePullback_map` as non-simp `rfl` unfolding lemmas, and have downstream proofs call them explicitly. The current uses are `rw [conePullback_map]` and `simp only [SheafedSpace.conePullback_obj, SheafedSpace.conePullback_map, …]`, so they do not depend on the simp attribute. Add `@[simp]` to `conePullback_obj`/`conePullback_map` stated against `conePullbackObj`/`conePullbackMap` instead, with `rfl` proofs. Also tag `conePullbackMap_id` and `conePullbackMap_comp` as `@[simp]` (the comp lemma is a `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` candidate). Then simp has one canonical form, and `map_id`/`map_comp` applied to the functor are not overridden by the full unfolding.
findings.benefit: `simp` on expressions like `(conePullback A S c).map (𝟙 i)` or `.map (a ≫ b)` then reaches the identity or composite normal form without a race with `Functor.map_id`/`Functor.map_comp`. It also stops leaking `triangleMap … sheafMate` terms with embedded `show` proofs into goals. Downstream users keep the readable `conePullbackMap` interface.

evidence.excerpt: conePullbackMap A S c (𝟙 i) = 𝟙 (conePullbackObj A S c i)
